statement: Bank of America research cited in the article says GPU performance drops sharply below 500GB of memory, framing the Rubin Ultra despec as a temporary engineering compromise rather than demand destruction.
why: If performance degrades steeply below 500GB, the lower configuration is unlikely to persist, which means the memory-content cut is a supply-side bottleneck rather than a downshift in accelerator demand.

impact.mechanism: A performance cliff below 500GB caps how far memory content can be cut, so the despec reads as a temporary supply constraint during qualification while underlying accelerator memory demand stays intact.

evidence.excerpt: Bank of America research cited: 'GPU performance drops sharply below 500GB', suggesting lower configurations represent a temporary engineering compromise rather than permanent demand destruction; the analysis notes this reflects a supply bottleneck during qualification delays.

confidence.basis: Sell-side note quoted inside a single secondary article; no primary filing, so capped at medium.

dispersion: conflicting same-key reports: magnitude 2 -> 1; sources: 24/7 Wall St., AMD Investor Relations
